findings.passage: Because voter suppression can happen both at the state and local level, as representative, I will continue my work to establish easy access to the ballot box and fight to overturn restrictive voter ID laws while expanding access to early and absentee voting.
findings.note: Issue page of her campaign site (Rep. Stacey Evans, GA House District 57). The page itself is undated. She says she will work to overturn restrictive voter ID laws and expand early and absentee voting.

findings.passage: I also believe that voter registration should be easy and permanent and that citizens should be able to vote at any precinct within their county lines.
findings.note: Same issue page. Says registration should be easy and permanent and voting should be allowed at any precinct in the county.

findings.passage: SB189 is an unnecessary bill that puts more burden on our local elections with new unfunded mandates, and attempts to fix an issue that is not there. This bill would allow for more mass voter challenges and could disqualify more voters.
findings.note: Her own legislative newsletter on SB 189 (2024), about voter-eligibility challenges. Related topic, not ID itself.

findings.passage: In particular, this bill would encourage citizen challenges to voter eligibility, which further strains our election workers.
findings.note: End-of-session newsletter on SB 189 (2024). She says it had some positive aspects but the negatives outweighed them.

findings.passage: Proponents of those pieces of legislation come to this well and say, ‘This is going to secure our elections,’ " Evans said during a debate in the state House. “Then the next year, we have to come back and open up the code again. So are you lying then or are you lying now? Is it now going to be the most secure?”
findings.note: Quoted by the Atlanta Journal-Constitution (April 2024 election-bill package story) from her House floor remarks on repeated election bills.
